sentences.text: The only known species, Cratoavis cearensis, belongs to the enantiornithines, a group of early birds. It is classified within the family Enantiornithes.

The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — is an articulated skeleton preserved with attached feathers, muscle tissue, and skin traces. This bird is characterized by having thinner skeletal structures compared to other enantiornithine birds.
The genus name means 'Bird of Crato', while the species name cearensis refers to the state of Ceará where the formation is located.
Its tail feathers are exceptionally long, reaching up to 30% longer than the total body length.
It is the first nearly complete Cretaceous bird skeleton discovered in South America.
Fish remains found near the holotype's intestine provide direct evidence that Cratoavis ate fish.
The fossil was found in the Early Cretaceous Araripe Basin in Ceará, Brazil. The genus name Cratoavis honors the Crato Formation where the specimen was discovered.
Cratoavis lived during the Late Aptian stage of the Early Cretaceous, between 125.45 and 112.6 million years ago. The fossil record for Cratoavis spans from 119.57 to 113.2 million years ago.

The fossil layers indicate a lake environment with still waters containing clay sediments, plant, fish, and insect fossils. Chemical analysis suggests the ancient lake waters were alkaline and hypersaline.
